prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: C[C@H](NCc1ccc(OCc2cccc(F)c2)cc1)C(N)=O
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL2039

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of human recombinant microsomal MAOB expressed in baculovirus infected BTI-TN-5B1- 4 cells using p-tyramine as substrate assessed as decrease in H2O2 production after 15 mins by amplex red-based fluorescence assay
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of human recombinant MAO-B expressed in insect cells using p-tyramine as substrate preincubated for 30 mins followed by substrate addition measured for 15 mins by resorufin dye-based fluorescence assay
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
INSUFFICIENT_INFO is not a valid response. You must commit to COMMENSURABLE or NOT_COMMENSURABLE.
If you lack direct evidence, make your best guess based on compound structure and target identity.
raw: {"call": "COMMENSURABLE", "confidence": 0.6, "error_class": "none", "reason": "Both assays measure IC50 of the same compound against human recombinant MAO-B expressed in insect cells using p-tyramine as substrate with a fluorescence-based readout (Amplex Red produces resorufin, so these are essentially the same detection method), and while the preincubation time differs (none specified vs 30 mins), for a reversible inhibitor the IC50 values should be comparable."}
